title: Best Dehumidifier for 3000 Sq Ft (2026): 2,500–3,000 Sq Ft
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for 2,500 to 3,000 Square Feet
dek: At 3,000 square feet, one portable stops being the obvious answer. Here's how to size it, and when to go whole-house.
description: The best 3000 sq ft dehumidifier depends on dampness and layout. Our picks cover big basements, open floors and whole homes from 2,500 to 3,000 sq ft.
intro: Choosing a **3,000 sq ft dehumidifier** is where sizing gets interesting. Below about 2,000 square feet, a single 50-pint portable handles most homes and basements. At 2,500 to 3,000 square feet, the answer depends on what those square feet actually are: one big open basement, two floors of living space, or a whole house with a damp lower level. The same number can call for one portable, two of them, or an installed whole-house unit.

To narrow it down, we started from the math in our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) — dampness first, then square footage, then ceiling height and moisture sources — and compared models on DOE and AHAM ratings, ENERGY STAR data, drainage and owner-reported reliability.
topPicksLead: For a whole 3,000 sq ft home, the **Aprilaire E080** is the best choice: it's rated for up to about 4,400 sq ft, carries ENERGY STAR's Most Efficient label and never needs a bucket emptied.

products.name: Aprilaire E080 Pro Whole-House Dehumidifier (80 Pints)
products.award: Best overall for a 3,000 sq ft home
pros: 80 pints a day for homes up to about 4,400 sq ft
Pro bundle adds a drain hose, spare filter and risers
cons: Needs a drain line, or a condensate pump bought separately
Ducted setups usually call for a pro install
products.whyWeLoveIt: Once you're drying 3,000 square feet across more than one level, a single machine tied into your ductwork beats a pair of portables you have to move, empty and maintain. The E080 is the right-sized step into Aprilaire's whole-house range: enough capacity for a typical 3,000 sq ft home with headroom, without paying for the bigger E100.
products.performance: Aprilaire rates it at 80 pints a day under AHAM conditions for homes up to about 4,400 square feet. That leaves comfortable margin at 3,000, so the unit runs long, steady cycles instead of straining. You set a target humidity and it switches on when the house rises above it. Designed and assembled in the USA, it has no tank at all — water leaves through a drain line.
products.notes: If your home has central air, tie it into the return so dried air reaches every room. Our [whole-house dehumidifier installation](/guides/whole-house-dehumidifier-installation/) guide walks through ducting and drainage, and our [best Aprilaire dehumidifier](/best/best-aprilaire-dehumidifier/) guide compares the full E-Series.

products.name: Midea Cube 50-Pint Smart Dehumidifier (MAD50S1QWT)
products.award: Best portable for one big open space
pros: ENERGY STAR rated at 49.67 pints a day on the DOE test
Rated for up to 4,500 sq ft, per Midea
4.2-gallon base tank empties far less often
Wi-Fi app plus Alexa and Google Assistant
cons: No pump, so the hose only drains downhill
products.whyWeLoveIt: If your 3,000 square feet is mostly one open basement with no doors between zones, a top-tier portable can do the job. The Cube 50 is the strongest 50-pint unit we know of for that, and its oversized base tank means fewer trips downstairs when there's no drain.
products.performance: ENERGY STAR lists it at 49.67 pints a day under the current DOE test, 2.01 liters per kWh and 515 kWh a year. Midea's 4,500 sq ft coverage claim assumes moderate dampness; in a very damp 3,000 sq ft basement, expect it to run long hours. The humidistat adjusts from 35% to 85%, and the app lets you confirm the far end of the basement is staying in range.
products.notes: Pair it with a separate hygrometer on the opposite side of the space. If the far reading stays high, you need a second unit, not a lower setpoint.

products.name: GoveeLife Smart Dehumidifier with Pump (H7152)
pros: Rated 50 pints a day at DOE-style 65°F, 60% conditions
Drains itself and dries its coil after shutting off
cons: Headline 137-pint figure is a hot, saturated maximum
Needs about 8 inches of clearance behind the intake
products.whyWeLoveIt: Large basements rarely have a floor drain in the right spot. This GoveeLife pushes water up and out through a 16-foot hose to a sink, window or sump, so a 3,000 sq ft space can run all season with nobody emptying anything.
products.performance: Govee's listing gives 50 pints a day at 65°F and 60% humidity — the same conditions as the DOE test — so you can compare it directly with the Midea. It's rated for up to 4,500 square feet. After shutdown, it pumps out the water left in its small reservoir and runs a drying cycle on the coil, a nice touch for a unit that sits in a damp space for months.
products.notes: See the full lineup in our [best Govee dehumidifier](/best/best-govee-dehumidifier/) guide, and more self-draining options in our [dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) picks.

products.whyWeLoveIt: Not every 3,000 sq ft home is damp. If yours just feels a little muggy in summer and smells faintly musty in the basement, a 35-pint unit is enough — and it uses noticeably less electricity across a long season.
products.performance: ENERGY STAR lists it at 35.82 DOE pints a day, 2.01 L/kWh and 378 kWh a year. Midea's current listing rates it for up to 3,500 square feet; earlier listings said 3,000. Either way, that claim assumes only moderate dampness, which matches the size guide: a moderately damp space over 2,000 square feet needs about 30 DOE pints or more.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for 3,000 sq ft

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. We compare capacity on like-for-like ratings (DOE 2019 for portables, AHAM for whole-house units), ENERGY STAR efficiency listings, coverage claims, drainage options and warranties, then read owner reviews for recurring failures and check CPSC recall records.

At this size, we weighted unattended running heavily. A 3,000 sq ft space can fill a portable's bucket more than once a day in summer, so every pick here can drain continuously, and two of them never need emptying at all.

sections.heading: What to look for in a 3,000 sq ft dehumidifier

items.label: Ratings you can compare
items.text: Portable pints should be DOE 2019 figures. Numbers measured at 80°F or 95°F run higher and can't be compared with them.

items.label: Coverage claims with a grain of salt
items.text: "Up to 4,500 sq ft" assumes moderate dampness and open airflow. Use the dampness table above, not the box.

items.label: Continuous drainage
items.text: A gravity hose to a floor drain, a built-in pump, or a whole-house unit plumbed to a drain line.

items.label: Efficiency
items.text: At this size, a unit can run 2,000+ hours a season. Check ENERGY STAR status and our [electricity cost guide](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/).

items.label: A plan for airflow
items.text: Interior doors and stairwells block a portable. If the space is divided, plan for a ducted unit or one portable per zone.

sections.heading: What "3,000 sq ft" on the box really means

blocks.text: Coverage figures aren't standardized. Brands pick them, usually assuming moderate dampness, 8-foot ceilings and open airflow. That's why a 35-pint Midea and a 50-pint unit from another brand can both claim several thousand square feet.
What about the Hisense 3,000 sq ft dehumidifier?

Hisense markets its 35-pint model for spaces up to 3,000 square feet. Like the Midea Cube 35, it suits a 3,000 sq ft home that's only moderately damp. For a very damp basement of that size, step up to a 50-pint unit. Our [best Hisense dehumidifier](/best/best-hisense-dehumidifier/) guide covers the lineup.

blocks.title: The two-hygrometer test
blocks.text: Put one hygrometer near the dehumidifier and another at the far end of the space. If they differ by more than about 5 points after a day of running, your unit isn't reaching the whole area.

For a whole 3,000 sq ft house, especially across several levels, the **Aprilaire E080** is the set-and-forget answer. If your square footage is one open basement, the **Midea Cube 50** does the job where there's a floor drain, and the **GoveeLife with Pump** where there isn't. If the space is only mildly damp, the **Midea Cube 35** saves energy. Rate the dampness before you shop; it matters more than the square footage.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for 3,000 sq ft?
faqs.a: About 35 DOE pints for a moderately damp space, 50 pints for a very damp one, and an installed 80–100 pint (AHAM) unit, or two portables, for a wet basement or a multi-level home.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for 2,500 square feet?
faqs.a: A 30–35 pint unit if it's only musty, or a 50-pint unit if you see condensation on walls or pipes. Move up a size for ceilings over 8 feet or a laundry room in the space.

faqs.q: Is one dehumidifier enough for 3,000 sq ft?
faqs.a: Yes, if it's a single open space or a ducted whole-house unit. A portable can't push dry air up a stairwell or through closed doors, so a home split into zones usually needs two portables or one installed system.

faqs.q: Is a 50-pint dehumidifier big enough for 3,000 sq ft?
faqs.a: For a very damp but open 3,000 sq ft basement, usually yes, though it will run long hours. For standing water or seepage, choose an installed 80–100 pint unit or add a second 50-pint portable.

faqs.q: Does Hisense make a 3,000 sq ft dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Yes. Hisense markets its 35-pint model for up to 3,000 square feet. It's a reasonable fit for a moderately damp space; a very damp basement of that size needs a 50-pint unit.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to dehumidify 3,000 sq ft?
faqs.a: ENERGY STAR lists the Midea Cube 50 at 515 kWh a year. At about 17 cents per kWh, that's under $100 a season. Wetter spaces, longer seasons and less efficient models cost more.
